newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds slip back after US production data.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds slip back after US production data.

text.p: Irish bonds slipped back in moderate trade as markets see-sawed following stronger than expected U.S. industry output data, dealers said.

"After the very strong gains we made yesterday a decline might have been expected even without bearish data from the U.S.," a dealer said. "As it is, the numbers have caused a negative tug on the market."

U.S. industrial production was shown to have risen 0.9 percent in March against a forecast rise of 0.6 forecast, while capacity utilisation was at its highest in two years. U.S. Treasuries skidded down following the news.

On the Irish market, at 1515 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was down 22 pence from Tuesday's close at 102.10 to yield 5.95 percent while the key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 was down 20 pence from the close at 108.75 to yield 6.70 percent.
Dealers said Irish bonds were yielding 137 basis points over Germany in the five-year area and 86 basis points over German bunds in the 10-year area, a widening of two basis points since yesterday.
"We're underperforming core Europe and gilts today," said a dealer.
On Tuesday bond markets around the globe benefited from softer than expected U.S. CPI data, with consumer prices rising just 0.1 percent in March versus a forecast rise of 0.2 percent.
The figures helped cool concerns about the possibility of a near-term interest rate hike to rein in the U.S. economy.
